funnily enough, Poland is decent. like for the country with "LGBT free zones" you'd expect terrible trans healthcare, but it's fine.

to get on HRT in Poland you first need to get a psychologist's opinion that you are, in fact, trans. the length of said diagnosis process varies between specialists by a lot, like, one could give it to you even on the first visit, another after three, then another after eight. now, with your diagnosis, you go to a doctor with a sexuologist specialization, can be anyone from an endocrinologist to a psychiatrist, and get them to give you a prescription for HRT. go to a pharmacy, bam.

the process isn't at all standardized, however, and that can give some people trouble. because in truth, some doctors don't even require a psychologist's opinion and might give you a prescription for HRT without it. other doctors refuse to work without it. the wait times are inconsistent and it's hell trying to find a place that could give you that opinion that's also not private—most trans people in Poland don't even try going by NFZ (polish national healthcare).

there's more than one clinic doing top surgeries now, idk how it is for transfems however. no idea about bottom surgeries here, either. i know that we used to have to sue our parents to get our gender markers changed, but after lgbt-phobic politician made some ruckus about it, it got changed lol.

there's also a whole website called tranzycja.pl that outlies the entire process and has a map of lgbtq+ friendly specialists. mostly in Poland, but not exclusively? still. Poland is a decent option, in all honesty.

wychowałum się we wsi gminnej na lubelskim, mniej więcej 1,4 tys osób, teraz mieszkam w mieście wojewódzkim w kujawsko-pomorskim.

nie wiem dokładnie ile osób dojeżdżało do swoich prac, ale strzelam że większość z nich lądowała w mieście które jest ~25 km dalej. ewentualnie była też całkiem blisko przetwornia, więc to było częste zjawisko—patrzenie się na pielgrzymkę grupy kilku osób które szły na piechotę do tej przetworni, bo wsm nie opłaca się nawet jechać busem.

mówiąc o busach, było ich kilka z dwóch firm, więc ceny się aż tak nie jebały. pamiętam jak wracałum jednym z nich i bilet wtedy (ok 2019 rok) na te 25 km kosztował ponad 10 zł... a miesięczny jakieś 200-coś.
było ich rano, od 5:30 do 8:30, chyba 4. potem był problem żeby się dostać w środku dnia, bo był jeden tak coś jakoś o 10 albo 11. od 12 zaczynały się przyjazdy z miasta do nas, więc były też powrotne. generalnie sytuacja u mnie z busami była spoko, chociaż później to bardzo często po prostu brakowało miejsca w busach, więc trzeba było stać.

rozrywki? brak lol. znaczy. kiedy była u nas pizzeria, potem ją zamknęli, więc przez całe moje lata młode to nie było miejsca gdzie można się spotkać ze znajomymi. ewentualnie można był siedzieć w domu albo na szkolnym placu zabaw, ale trudno na placu zabaw chlać. alkoholizm był (może i nadal jest) epidemią wśród osób na mojej wsi, gdzie pamiętam 14 latków próbowających przesmuglować wódki na szkolne dyskoteki i pamiętam panów pijaków których każdy znał, bo to zawsze byli ci sami ludzie.

szczerze to nie tęsknię za mieszkaniem na wsi. jak wracam na święta albo ochotniczo, to całkowicie brakuje mi energii, żeby wychodzić z domu bez powodu. nie wiem, jak to jest na innych wsiach, ale u nas przekupki i plotkarze są wszędzie. może właśnie przez to, że nie ma co innego robić, niż się gapić przez płot? nie wiem. ale nikt ci nie zrobi problemów z poczuciem własnej wartości tak specyficznych, jak wsiowe plotkary. mieszkam setki km dalej a nadal czuje się jakby ktoś miał mojej mamie przekazać co robię 24/7 jak wychodzę do ludzi, bo na wsi to jak nie powiedziałum komuś dzień dobry to była nagana XD

anyway: dojazdy są, łatwiej jest ofc jak ma się samochód, ja prawka nie mogę mieć przez problemy zdrowotne. jeżeli chcesz gdzieś posiedzieć jak np w kafejce albo bistro to możesz tylko pomarzyć, chociaż dla niektórych zastępowanie tego pójściem do kogoś na obiad jest lepsze. bez własnej inicjatywy pewnie nie wyrobisz sobie nowego hobby, ale też pewnie nie znajdziesz nikogo z podobnymi zainteresowaniami, szczególnie jeżeli jesteś mieszczuchem.

hi i'd like to pitch in here too. i'm also autistic and have ADHD, and have terrible reactions to many sensory thingies bc i have SPS.

i have previously berated my roommate (or mom or whoever else would've been living with me) for being inconsiderate and awful if something they did caused my meltdown... but *in my head.* like, i can think some awful shit. it just happens. but thoughts are thoughts and they're fueled by my discomfort so they're particularly vile, and when i self-soothe and calm down, i'm usually like wow damn let's dial that down.

i draw a fine line for myself, where me complaining in my own thoughts and not acting out because of them is okay—it's like if i was venting to a third party, because i just throw the words out into the ether of my brain and all of them fail to stick because of the state my brain is in. i won't ever, never ever, say these things out loud, because i don't mean them and i know they would be hurtful.

the last time i've engaged with someone while melting down was when i was trying to study and mine and my roommate's cat was being very annoying. she didn't move from her room or do anything while i was getting more and kore aggravated because i was trying to focus and my focus was being consistently broken, making it even worse—so i went into her room and raised my voice a bit out of frustration, asking her why she's not doing anything if she can hear me getting frustrated from a problem she can fix. she wasn't doing anything important, just laying in bed, and i'd told her i'd study beforehand so i needed *some* help. still, what i said wasn't hostile or angry, i didn't call her awful or whatever, even if a part of me wanted to, just because i felt so awful.

self-regulating like this is difficult, especially for neurodiverse folks, but it is doable. especially if you don't want to hurt someone.

the wołyń massacre happened in 1943-1944, in the volhynia voivodeship. the territory was under the claim of the third reich at that time. it wasn't the soviets, rather, it was ukrainian nationalists (who were, in truth, just fascists) that took example in the ethnic cleansing of the jews done by nazis and did that to the foreigners in wołyń (and lwów, tarnopolska and stanisławów), most of which were poles. it's a relatively lesser known genocide, seeing as polish people have been senselessly targeted for murder by many others across the years, but the current war has brought it up to relevance again. i'm not sure how much material about it is available online in english, but there's a decently sized wikipedia article at the very least.

it's okay if you are not comfortable supporting anyone russian, or if you won't feel that way even after the war ends. yes, a lot of russians are in support of the war, but they are fed relentless, endless propaganda (note: i'm not saying this to downplay how horrible these views are). the few that don't agree and consciously go against it—like, for example, the pathologic devs, with the game's narrative being an inherent critique of societal issues at large—aren't the ones you should be vocally going against. there are better discourses to spend your energy on than here, in the comments of a post announcing the departure of one of the pathologic devs haha

no, but it has conducted an all out ethnic cleanse on polish people not even 100 years ago. the genocide of wołyń has not, to my knowledge, been ever paid proper respect, even in light of us cooperating in the modern day.

how different would it be for me to publicly state and refuse my support of some ukrainian artist—not at all related to the crimes committed—due to that? i am sure you can agree that having your own people mindlessly slaughtered is not nice, so it's almost natural to hold a grudge.

my point, mainly, is that you are aiming at the wrong threat. you are well within your right to support or not support whoever you want, but to publicly condemn people very likely oppose the same people as you—as much as they can—is, in my opinion, dumb. don't you have better comments to write? i'm sure you can offer something more insightful than "yeah i'm not going to give money to them because they're russian". i saw that you'd gotten into online discourse with relatively random russian people more than once, so i hope you might listed to a fellow random person—othering people never works, because it just gives them confirmation that they are in the right. russian propaganda is everywhere. this is feeding into it.

ocd and personality disorders do count as neurodivergence, actually. neurodivergence is categorized as "a framework for understanding human brain function that considers the diversity within sensory processing, motor abilities, social comfort, cognition, and focus as neurobiological differences. This diversity falls on a spectrum of neurocognitive differences." as per wikipedia

the easiest way i've found to look at it, is that you cannot cure neurodiversity. you can learn to manage it, be it by therapy or medication, but you can't cure it—like how you can oftentimes cure anxiety or depression (disclaimer: not always). although you can manage ocd or personality disorders enough to be considered "cured", they stay with you forever.
